title: Hybrid SPACE Hardness of the SPACE Family
summary: Under the stated parameter bounds, SPACE is conjectured to satisfy hybrid SPACE hardness; proving or refuting this, including for SPACE256, remains open.

formal_statement.body: For $\mathrm{SPACE}$ with block size $n_a$, establish or refute the conjecture that $\mathrm{SPACE}$ satisfies $(t,\lambda,q,t_{\mathrm{lif}})$-hybrid SPACE hardness for $\lambda=(128-n_a)2^{n_a-2}$, $t+t_{\mathrm{lif}}<2^{128}$, and $q<2^{128}-\lfloor\lambda/128\rfloor$. In particular, for the instantiation $\mathrm{SPACE256}$ with $n_a=16$, determine whether $\mathrm{SPACE256}$ satisfies $(t,\lambda,q,t_{\mathrm{lif}})$-hybrid SPACE hardness for $\lambda=(256-16)\times 2^{16-2}$, $t+t_{\mathrm{lif}}<2^{128}$, and $q<2^{256}-\lfloor\lambda/256\rfloor$.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key cryptanalysis of the SPACE block-cipher family under hybrid SPACE hardness.
parameters: n_a: block size of SPACE, fixed to 16 for the SPACE256 instantiation
t, lambda, q, and t_lif: parameters of hybrid SPACE hardness subject to the stated equalities and upper bounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute hybrid SPACE hardness for SPACE under the stated bounds, including whether SPACE256 satisfies it.

citations.label: A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs

progress.summary: The source presents SPACE as an expected example satisfying hybrid SPACE hardness rather than as a proved result. The open task is to establish or refute the claim under the stated bounds, particularly for SPACE256.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., A Modular Approach to the Incompressibility of Block-Cipher-Based AEADs
